sentences.text: Priohybodus was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish that includes modern sharks and rays.
It holds the distinction of being the first hybodontiform shark discovered with fully serrated cutting edges on its teeth.
This predator hunted fish and large vertebrates, using its specialized teeth to grasp and cut its prey.
Taxonomically, the genus is grouped with Secarodus and Planohybodus within the informal group Priohybodontines.
Priohybodus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Albian stages, spanning the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous periods.
Fossils found in the Late Jurassic Mugher Mudstone of Ethiopia reveal a wide distribution across Gondwana, including Saharan Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and South America.
Research suggests that the enameloid structure of Priohybodus arambourgi differs from that of modern sharks despite their similar external tooth morphology.
